prior_importants.description: `lstatSync(path, { throwIfNoEntry: false })` only suppresses ENOENT. A directory under `src/` that can be listed but not searched (mode `0644`/`0444`) makes `lstat` of each child throw EACCES. `readModuleMap` then throws, and the whole Decisions sheet, timeline included, returns 500 "The store could not be read." on every request and poll.
The treemap legend says "(darker: 1, 2–3, 4 or more)", but in the dark theme --debt-0..--debt-3 run from dark to light, so dark-mode readers see the shading backwards.
The treemap escaping test's group sums to Infinity (1e308 + 1e308), so squarify draws nothing; removing escapeHtml from the group-label <text> (chart.utils.ts:452) passes the whole suite.
The "filling the box" test checks areas and bounds but not overlap, so a layRow that never advances `rest` (cells all stacked at the origin) still passes it and every treemap test.

findings.description: The treemap tests check each cell's width and height but never its position. A mutant that lays every group's cells from (0,0) still passes the whole suite, for example `squarify(group.leaves, { ...box, x: 0, y: 0 })` at chart.utils.ts:423. Under it, files are drawn outside their group's outline. A squarify case with a box away from the origin would catch it, or a check that each cell sits inside its group's rect.

The test for module order by newest record can't fail on the wrong order. In its fixture, src/core holds both the newest record and the most records, so a mutant that orders modules by record count still passes. A fixture where the newest record sits in the smaller module would separate the two.

The DecisionSheetRecord JSDoc says "every string through `oneLine`", but `session` and `when` never go through it. `session` is checked against SESSION_ID_PATTERN and `when` is built from an ISO date, so a reader could credit oneLine for making those two fields safe.

The comment above `visit` says it "says why it was not" counted, but it records no reason: it only increments `map.unread`. Suggested wording: "Counts one plain file, or tallies it as unread; false once a cap is reached."
The comment `// A file over the cap is never opened.` only restates the `stat.size > MAX_FILE_BYTES ? undefined : …` ternary below it. general.md §Comments says inline comments explain why, not what.

`NO_FILE = '(no file named)'` copies the same constant in web-dashboard-debt.service.ts:35, so the label can drift between the Debt and Decisions sheets. It could move to web-dashboard-sheet.utils.ts beside `oneLine`.

process_issues.description: The conventions reviewer did not read docs/conventions/testing.md. It also did not read chart.utils.ts or the test files line by line, so testing-convention compliance and most of chart.utils.ts went unchecked.

The simplicity reviewer read only the two new service files. It did not review the chart.utils.ts hunks (framed, squarify, layRow, groupCells, toneLevel) or web-dashboard.service.ts for oversized structure.
The guards reviewer could not list main's ADRs under the CI sandbox, so it confirmed ADR number 0167 is unique only in the checkout. scripts/adr-index.sh was not run.
